management_notes: Churchill Resources' management team has assembled a credible multi-property land position in NL's antimony-gold belt — the TSXV-approved Golden Baie option (Canstar Resources), combined with Frost Cove and Black Raven, demonstrates systematic district consolidation. However, two significant concerns keep the score at 2. First, the May 2026 data-correction incident (restated Frost Cove drill results) has not been neutralised by a subsequent clean, independently audited data package; the reputational damage persists in the sector. Second, insider ownership is not documented in available public filings; the April 29, 2026 interim MD&A (the most recent cap-table source) does not provide a management/director ownership breakdown. The 316.7M issued shares outstanding reflects a history of serial dilutive financings with no disclosed insider participation rate to offset the optics.
geology_notes: High-grade antimony mineralisation is confirmed across the district. Post-correction 2025 drill results at Black Raven / southern Frost Cove include best intercepts of 7.25% Sb over 1.98 m, 6.44% Sb over 2.06 m, 4.84% Sb over 1.00 m, and 3.94% Sb over 1.60 m. A secondary gold-silver system at depth returned 5.89 g/t AuEq over 1.00 m at Black Raven, adding polymetallic optionality. The Beaver Brook occurrence (9.46% Sb / 35.5 g/t Au / 1,118 g/t Ag at surface) 1.2 km north of the historic Frost Cove mine extends the district footprint. The four-property portfolio (Frost Cove North, Frost Cove South/Black Raven, Beaver Brook, Golden Baie) constitutes a genuine district-scale exploration story in Newfoundland. The NI 43-101 technical report on file is dated August 1, 2023; no mineral resource estimate has been declared. All resource fields remain null. Score of 3 reflects exceptional grades and developing district scale, constrained by absence of a compliant resource estimate and the unresolved credibility impact of the data correction.

Shares issued outstanding: 316,681,940; shares fully diluted: 342,756,940 — sourced directly from the April 29, 2026 interim MD&A (extracted JSON sha256: f48119422ed45e5221bbb4bc336ee2176965c42d73986bf3a72af32ac4435736). The option pool of 23,450,000 represents approximately 7.4% of issued shares — material but within sector norms for a company at this stage. The structural constraint is the absolute share count: at 316.7M basic shares, generating meaningful per-share value requires a declared resource large enough to support a multi-hundred-million-dollar NAV. Score of 2 reflects this dilution overhang.
catalyst_notes: Multiple near-term catalysts remain live across the 2026 program. Nine northern Frost Cove holes were awaiting assay as of the May 22, 2026 corporate update (most recent confirmed public disclosure); those results represent the immediate binary event for the stock. The 2026 Golden Baie program (TSXV-approved) includes airborne geophysics, systematic trenching/channel sampling, and a drill campaign — a multi-quarter news pipeline. The strategic macro backdrop remains highly supportive: China's antimony export restrictions (in force since late 2024) continue to sustain elevated Sb pricing and Western government demand for domestic supply. A maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate — no timeline has been disclosed publicly — would be the step-change re-rating catalyst. All three web fetches for this run were blocked by HTTP 403 errors; no new public releases were confirmed between May 22, 2026 and this scorecard date (June 18, 2026). Score of 3 reflects live, near-term news flow constrained by the absence of a confirmed imminent catalyst.
acquisition_notes: No formal resource precludes quantitative P/NAV analysis; nav_per_share is null. The qualitative acquisition case is supported by: (a) confirmed high-grade antimony intercepts across multiple targets in an underexplored Canadian jurisdiction; (b) a consolidating land position across Newfoundland's antimony belt; (c) China's structural antimony export ban creating durable demand for Western supply; and (d) a shallow peer set — North American antimony exploration-stage companies are extremely scarce, elevating each one's strategic optionality. The gold-silver system at Black Raven and the surface high-grade discovery at Beaver Brook add multi-commodity appeal. Comparable transaction context: Perpetua Resources (Kinross strategic agreement, Idaho antimony-gold) and European critical-mineral M&A demonstrate strategic acquirers pay premiums beyond conventional NAV multiples for assured supply chains. Score of 3 reflects strong strategic optionality constrained by the absence of a declared resource to anchor transaction valuation.
